source_read: PDF pp. 1-3 (PDFs/MDMA/Marseille_2025_CritiqueCostEffectiveness.pdf): read in full, including the interdisciplinarity, CRediT, generative-AI, conflict-of-interest and data-availability statements and the 13 references; all three pages rendered at 110 dpi. For one cross-check, the author information and competing-interest statement of MAPP1 (Mitchell et al., 2021) read on nature.com in my own browser tab. Step 1 (blind extraction) not run this round, per the round brief.

design.note: A commentary; narrative-review fits better than modelling, since no model is described (only outputs are reported).

instrument.note: none-applicable with the editors' narrative-review checklist.

key_findings.note: The 1st paragraph ends at the top of the right column with the SSRIs and the trial's three 8-hour sessions with two clinicians.
p. 1, 2nd paragraph of the section. The source says 'in our study' after citing both earlier analyses (2020, 2022); which one gave 11,537 dollars is not stated.
Ends at the top of p. 2, left column. The ratio's five-year horizon is inferable from 'the five-year horizon used in the Lykos study' (p. 1).
The threshold argument cites the authors' own 2015 paper (Marseille et al., 2015).

12,000 dollars per dose, three dosing sessions, 36,000 for the regimen, therapy excluded; 3.8 years (2022 analysis); about 8.4 years; 160 dollars per QALY over five years at 10,500; dominant below 10,320.
The 3rd paragraph begins at the foot of the left column of p. 2 and continues in the right column.

Six paragraphs in the section; the 2nd to 6th run from the right column of p. 2 to the left column of p. 3. The source frames fewer sessions as conceivable; 'untested assumption' is the card's fair gloss.

reporting_issues.note: Earleywine et al. (2025, p. 1, Introduction 1st paragraph) does report effect sizes over one standard deviation and numbers needed to treat below four for prolonged exposure, cognitive processing therapy and EMDR, citing Cusack et al. (2016).

risk_of_bias.note: I agree with every domain and the overall.

domains.domain: Reliance on the authors' own studies
domains.note: High is right, and the reliance runs deeper than the models: the second author appears to be the first author of both phase 3 trials whose effects both models take as given (see 'missed').

domains.domain: Balance of evidence on the cost-effectiveness of MDMA-assisted therapy

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial. The abstract's 'or even cost-saving' rests on the authors' own model at a drug price below 10,320 dollars and on a base-case comparator with no health gain, neither of which the abstract says.

missed: Identity of the second author, which strengthens the card's flag: her two UCSF departments (Neurology; Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences) are exactly the two printed for Jennifer M. Mitchell, first author of MAPP1 (publisher HTML, author information), whose competing-interest statement there records MAPS PBC funding for the study. She is very probably the first author of both trials whose effects both the sponsor's and the critics' models take at face value; the commentary does not say so.

Field correction (exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route): '11,537 dollars in the authors' 2022 model' goes beyond the source, which says 'in our study' after citing both the 2020 and the 2022 analyses.

Cross-claim pointer: this is the only source read in the batch stating that follow-up data beyond 18 weeks exist and were used (17 months from MAPP2 and MPLONG, in the sponsor's model). The efficacy and contested claims' 'no outcome after 18 weeks is reported' stays true of the papers read, but the existence of the MPLONG data could be named.
